name: Tallinn University
summary: Tallinn humanities and social sciences university of about 7,000 students; six English-taught bachelor's in media, liberal arts, politics and law.

ib.text: No IB points or subjects are asked: places go on an interview, portfolio or exam, with 65 of 100 as the floor. IB graduation documents count as proof of English. Send the Diploma and transcript.

programmes.name: Audiovisual Media
programmes.about: Storytelling for film and television, from documentary and fiction to music videos. You choose a creative module (writing, directing, producing) or a technical one (camera, sound, editing, colour) and finish with a practical film.
programmes.ib: Portfolio, two creative assignments and an interview decide; choose the creative or the technical module when applying.
programmes.selectionNote: Portfolio, CV and letter 30%, two creative assignments 35%, interview 35%; 75+ points guarantees a place. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Crossmedia
programmes.about: Stories that move between platforms, from film to television to live performance, combining audiovisual content with print, events, apps, games and social media, plus the business side of media.
programmes.ib: A three-minute audiovisual CV, a creative assignment and an interview decide; interviews can be held online.
programmes.selectionNote: Interview 50%, audiovisual CV 30%, creative assignment 20%. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Liberal Arts in Humanities
programmes.about: A three-year humanities degree that starts from shared foundations and moves to your own path through specialist modules, electives, project work and an internship across culture, history, language and society.
programmes.ib: A 500-word motivation letter, then an interview that includes discussing an academic text you read beforehand.
programmes.selectionNote: Interview and text discussion 70%, motivation letter 30%; minimums apply to each part. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Liberal Arts in Social Sciences
programmes.about: An interdisciplinary base across sociology, political science, international relations, economics, law and psychology, with research methods, an internship and a project; you shape your own direction through electives.
programmes.ib: The exam is a 20-minute interview on your CV, motivation and a short article you prepare; 65 of 100 is the minimum.
programmes.selectionNote: Admission exam is one interview scored out of 100; 65 points is the minimum. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Politics and Governance
programmes.about: How political systems, institutions and policy work, with options in comparative politics, public administration, global governance, European politics and international relations.
programmes.ib: The exam is a 20-minute interview on your CV, motivation and a short article you prepare; 65 of 100 is the minimum.
programmes.selectionNote: Admission exam is one interview scored out of 100; 65 points is the minimum. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Law
programmes.about: European and international law at the core, taught through case analysis, legal writing, group work, mock trials and moot court; no earlier legal study is needed.
programmes.ib: The exam is a 20-minute interview on your CV, motivation and a short article you prepare; 65 of 100 is the minimum.
programmes.selectionNote: Admission exam is one interview scored out of 100; 65 points is the minimum. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: The 2027/28 fee table says fees are the same for all students regardless of citizenship; every bachelor's here is fee-paying.
Applicants under 18 at the start of studies may be refused admission.
Two full tuition reductions a year go to the top-ranked entrants across the six English-taught bachelor's degrees.
